correctness.rationale: Independently generated the twenty stated radius-√3 vertices and computed |u·(v×w)| for each of the 4845 unordered distinct quadruples, using rational coefficients of 1 and √5 and exact signs. Converting to the 1,φ basis gives all eleven increasing determinant levels and precisely the printed multiplicities, including 495 zeros. I counted incidences at each of the twenty vertices; each table is the global histogram divided by five, consistent with transitivity and four incidences per quadruple. The ten maxima have all six squared edge lengths equal to 8 and volume 8/3, and the 120 next-largest cases have volume 4φ/3, giving the stated relative gap. Exact weighted sums gave both advertised moments; independently, XᵀX=20I₄ and Cauchy–Binet give sum Δ²=160000. The positive gap is only for vertex-supported tetrahedra. Replay: python3 -B /workspace/branches/independent-checks/record1.py.

value.rationale: This is the full volume distribution for the natural finite sampling of tetrahedra in a Platonic vertex set. The table answers how frequent degeneracy is, separates the maximizers from the next shell by a sharp gap, and permits exact averages; a compound or maximum theorem cannot provide those data. The finite scope is useful as a benchmark for discrete polyhedral volume questions. That judgment credits the frozen record’s full distribution, not a claim of priority, the later restatement, or the already classical top row.
